topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture series, personal background, and core learning outcomes concerning environmental carcinogens and cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer causation by evaluating the relative roles of intrinsic cellular mutations, microenvironmental factors, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological trends.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and infectious carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the specific biological and molecular mechanisms through which pathogens, dietary toxins, radiation, xenobiotics, and tumour promoters drive neoplastic development and tissue-specific vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for detecting and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to identify and confirm carcinogen exposure and mutagenic risk.

topics.label: Summary of carcinogen exposure and risk assessment
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarising key takeaways regarding environmental cancer risks and personal risk–benefit decision-making.
